note: Overlapping low-efficiency opening range with no swings/H2-L2 and price pinned near EMA: no qualifying 2nd entry appears; staying flat all window is correct, not passivity.
Lone 50-pt climactic bear spike into session low followed by a weak 3-bar bounce inside a two-sided range — no follow-through case, so no entry either direction. Correct to wait.

Gap-down AIS day but the down move was choppy with heavy bar overlap (efficiency ~0.2-0.55, always-in flipping to neutral bars 10-12) and oversized/climactic bear bars (bars 15-16 both ~14pt outside/trend bars on lows). No clean 2nd-entry short set up with-trend, and bull bars (9, 17) were just bounces in chop. Standing aside all session was the correct read — a bear bias alone doesn't justify chasing extended or climactic bars, and a choppy range with no confirmed pullback structure offers no edge.

Double top was at the session high but the bot entered short on the break of the session low (long-held support) — selling the bottom of a choppy range. In an extreme TR, short the double top near the high targeting the low, or stand aside; do not short the neckline break at the range low.

After a choppy gap-down trading range, a clean 3-bar bull spike reclaiming above EMA is a valid long, but entering late in the spike (bar 14, price already ~6903 after running from 6869) buys near exhaustion into the prior range's overhead supply — the pullback tagged the tight ~8.5pt stop. Consider requiring a first pullback (2nd entry) rather than entering on spike continuation when the move has already traveled 30+ pts off the low.

Gap-up that immediately sells off into an overlapping low-efficiency range (efficiency ~0.20, overlap ~0.64, alternating SH/SL swings) offers no clean KB setup — always-in kept flipping (AIS bars 3-11, neutral/AIL bars 12-19). Correct read is to sit out the whole opening window rather than fade chop; bars 20-23 rightly gated too_late_in_window.

Gap-down reversed into a persistent overlapping bull channel; bot stayed flat all day citing choppy texture and buying-at-highs. In a confirmed always-in-long grind, look harder for a valid 2nd-entry long (H2/L2 pullback to EMA) rather than defaulting to no_trade — zero trades in a 35pt trend is under-participation, not caution.

Bilateral range: gap-down open, swings ping-pong (LL 6957 / HH 6989), efficiency <0.4, always-in neutral. Correctly took zero trades. Doji signal bars (b7,9,16), oversized reversal chase (b8 18.25pt off session low), and a near-magnet short (b12 closing 1.75pt above prior low) were all properly rejected. In extreme two-sided chop with no completed MTR, no signal is a valid outcome.

Strong AIL bull spike-to-channel day, gap +46.5, EMA rising, price held well above EMA bars 1-17. Bot skipped every long and traded nothing. Next time on a clean always-in-long day, treat the first shallow pullback that holds above a rising EMA as a valid 2nd-entry long rather than waiting for a perfect bar — don't let 'too early / chase / near high' objections stack into total inaction.

The bot passed the entire opening bear spike (bars 5-11) because every bar was a with-trend sell into an extended move with no 2nd-entry short pullback and no completed MTR for a countertrend long. Standing aside a fast one-directional spike you didn't get positioned in early is correct — chasing bar 6/7/11 (large bars closing on lows / new session lows) would have been climax-chasing into oversized bars. No pullback short setup ever formed.

After the spike stalled ~6956, bars 12-19 became choppy two-sided rotation around a flattening EMA (bull/bear bars alternating, AI flipping AIS/neutral, closes mid-range). Correctly took nothing: no clean KB setup, magnets (flat EMA, session mid) nearby, and signal bars were dojis/mid-range. Bar-19 cutoff then closed the window. Doing nothing in a structureless range is the disciplined outcome, not a missed trade.

setup: no_trade discipline in a post-spike overlapping range
note: Gap-up spike that immediately rolls over and starts overlapping (overlap ~0.6, no follow-through, always-in flipping bar-to-bar) is a trading range, not a trend. Tempting bull trend bars near the session high (bar12/13/15/19) are chases into the top of the range or into magnets, not 2nd-entry setups. Staying flat and eating no losses is the correct, repeatable outcome here — don't manufacture a fade or a breakout entry just to be in.

Range-fade short at the top of a tight overlapping range was sound in direction, but the stop was set below the true session high (7005) rather than above it, so a retest of the high stopped it out at ~1R. For double-top fades: stop a tick above the higher top, and confirm target keeps R:R comfortably >1 before entering.

Gap-up (+40pt) that reverses into a tight two-sided TR (efficiency <0.1, overlap ~0.7, oscillating a ~17pt band around EMA) has no trend to trade WITH and no clean 2nd-entry against a magnet-rich range. Correct to take zero trades; doji-mid-range and too-late gates did their job. Don't force a fade or a breakout stop here — the range is the whole session.

setup: spike-and-channel long (breakout of morning range high)
note: On a gap-down two-sided range day, a 3-bar bull spike off the session low that runs into the top of the morning range (here entry 6903.75 vs range/session high ~6905) is prone to failing right at that range high. The range high is a magnet sitting between entry and target — require a completed break-and-close above the range before buying, or lean toward fading back into the range instead of chasing the breakout.

AIL grind-up from open with overlapping shallow pullbacks: no clean 2nd-entry signal bar ever formed (pullback bars were bear/doji or price was already extended above EMA). Standing aside all day here is acceptable process, but flag if this pattern of no-fills on genuine trend days recurs — may need a tight-channel entry (H1/L1 or small-pullback 2nd entry) tuned for shallow grinds.

Rule-compliant with-trend pullback long on a strong gap-up trend day, stopped by a deeper pullback. Entry sat ~23 pts above a lagging EMA; on such extended gap-up days the pullback can reach toward the EMA and trip a tight with-trend stop. Not a rule error — a good-process loss. Next time on similar extended trend days, note stop room vs. distance to EMA, but keep taking with-trend 2nd-entry pullbacks.

Gap-up early bull spike that immediately gives way to a broad two-sided grind (high overlap, low efficiency, swings ping-ponging ~6987-7006) is a no-trade regime. Spike with no clean pullback + range at the top = wait; don't manufacture an entry into the middle of chop.

On a two-sided range day already showing climax bear bars, don't sell the bottom of the range on an L2 channel pullback — this short entered near the session low after two oversized bear bars and was reversed hard back through entry to a new high. Require R:R>=1 and treat range lows as buy-not-sell zones absent a clean breakout+follow-through.

After a long two-sided range resolves into 5+ consecutive bull trend bars closing near highs (tight AIL channel), a 2nd-entry pullback long into the channel is a high-quality setup — new session highs mean no magnet overhead capping the first target. Waiting out the range before engaging paid off.

Gap-up that opens at the high and chops two-sided: don't force early signals through the noise (correctly skipped the bar5 oversized climax bar and the bar9 doji/inside bar). When always-in leans short and price stacks lower highs at a falling 20-EMA, a 2nd-entry pullback short into a fresh session low is a valid low-risk entry.

Rising EMA + AIL flag on a gap-up, but overlapping bars = trading range (bot flagged it bars 6-10). Buying the breakout near the top of that range failed. AIL hint != trend; treat a breakout in an acknowledged two-sided range as suspect unless there's a strong spike bar + follow-through.

With-trend H2 pullback that was mechanically clean but filled at the exact fresh session high on a two-sided day. Even a valid 2nd-entry buy struggles when it enters right into the session-high magnet on a range day — location matters, not just setup name.

After a long two-sided range resolves and always_in flips to AIL with a clean bull skeleton (HL->HH->HL) and rising EMA, a late-window channel-pullback long into the breakout can pay ~1R even on a chop day. Waiting for the AIL flip beat forcing trades in the 7046-7063 muck.

Gap-up, rising-EMA bull channel; H1 pullback long entered on a strong bar ~15pt above the pullback low, near the top of the only leg. Trend stalled into a two-sided range and stopped for -1R. Rule-compliant loss; note that on tight/low-efficiency gap-up sessions the first leg often tops into a range, so entries chasing a strong breakout bar and targets set beyond the fresh session high carry extra fade risk.
On a clean AIL day, sitting out a tight two-sided open and taking the first H1/H2 pullback once the HL skeleton is clear worked — patience through the grind paid off with a 1.7R winner.

Buying the pullback after a 3-bar bull spike that was already ~16pts above EMA got stopped. Legit setup, but note the extension: entries this far above EMA into a spike have less room before mean-reversion. Single sample — just track it, don't add a rule.

Gap-up AIL day where price had already topped at the session high and gone sideways. Pullback-long buy stop fired ~1pt below the session high (7417.5); it stalled at that magnet and reversed to the stop. Next time: when a stop entry sits just below the session high/other magnet, require price to clear the magnet or scale out near it — don't target well beyond a magnet the trade hasn't broken.

AIL gap-down recovery: pullback long entered near the top of a mature bull leg, ~5pt below the session-high magnet with 11.5pt risk. Recovery stalled and rotated into a trading range, stopping the trade. Process was sound (AIL, KB setup, risk/RR OK) — this is a normal loss, but note the thin room to the first magnet on a leg that had already run 47pt.

AIL day (gap +24, rising EMA, HH/HL skeleton). After a climactic ~52pt spike into a new session high, the bot did NOT chase the spike bars (14-16 all no_trade) but waited for the pullback to complete and took the with-trend 2nd entry on bar17, target beyond the prior session high. Clean patience-after-spike model to repeat.

Buying the H1/H2 resumption after a strong AIL bull spike into a shallow 2-legged pullback is textbook and correct. Stop was below the pullback low (~11pt risk); a slightly deeper-than-expected pullback stopped it before the trend resumed. Don't tighten or abandon this setup on one stop-out — the entry logic was sound.

Two-sided opening range on an AIL day capped by yday high 7574. Correct play: skip the in-range new-high stop entries jammed into the magnet (bars 9/11), wait for a higher low + rising EMA + AIL alignment, then take the trend-resumption long once price clears the magnet. Target ~12pts hit.

In a slow AIL grind with heavy bar overlap (~0.36) and a very tight session range, a pullback-breakout long that clears am_high has weak follow-through — the grind reverses on you as easily as it extends. Entry was rules-valid (AIL, KB setup, risk/RR fine); loss is normal. If anything, in these overlapping micro-grinds expect lower hit-rate and don't read one stop-out as a signal to change process.

setup: breakout-mode long (spike stop entry above tight PM range)
note: After a long tight two-sided afternoon range, five consecutive bull trend bars closing in the upper range with rising EMA is a valid strong-spike stop-entry long to a new session high. R:R ~1, no magnet overhead, hit target. Sitting out the chop first was the key discipline.

In an established AIL tight bull channel, wait for the first shallow bear pullback (bar 11) then take the 2nd-entry long off the pullback low — buying the channel dip rather than the highs kept risk tight (5pt stop) and caught the resumption to a clean +1.21R target.

After a clean multi-bar bear spike drives a new session low following a two-sided open, entering a 2nd-entry short WITH always_in and holding to a measured target worked. Patience through the choppy open (bars 1-6) preserved capital for the one high-quality signal.

AIS afternoon grinding down from a rejected session-high magnet (7645) with a falling EMA (slope ~-1.4). A 2nd-entry pullback short WITH the always-in, ~4pt stop, target at the extending session low, ran to target for +1.5R. When the day is one-sided AIS off a clear magnet rejection, take the channel pullback and let it work; then correctly stand down once it flattens into a two-sided range.

On a gap-up always-in-long day, two consecutive strong bull trend bars (closes ~0.95) justify a with-the-spike stop entry even without a 2nd-entry pullback; keep risk modest and target the measured move. Watch that the entry isn't chasing the oversized spike bar itself (bar 6 was 9.25pts) — here entry was on the next bar, which was fine.

With-trend bear pullback short taken right after a climactic spike + multi-bar low stall. Rules were followed and it lost to a reversal. Remember: a 4-bar pullback that can't extend the spike low, coming off an oversized climax bar, is where with-trend breakout shorts most often fail — prefer waiting for a clearer 2nd-entry or a resumption bar over selling the first new-low poke.

A 4-bar bear spike off a failing big gap-up looked like spike-and-channel but resolved into a two-sided TR (efficiency ~0.01, overlap ~0.6). Breakout shorts near the middle of what becomes a tight range get chopped; the low efficiency/high overlap developing early is the tell. Process was fine — just flag TR risk when a 'spike' fails to extend and bars start overlapping heavily.

Don't sell the breakout at the low of an established two-sided range sitting on the session-low support magnet — trading-range breakouts lack follow-through and get trapped back up. If bars just before were always_in neutral with high overlap, treat a fresh extreme-of-range signal as low-probability.

Choppy two-sided opening on a gap-up bull-trend day resolved upward. Waiting patiently through ~15 overlapping bars and taking the opening-range-high breakout (with always-in long, EMA well below, no magnet before target) worked. Don't force entries inside the range while always_in and texture disagree.

With-trend bear channel-pullback short, sound structure (10pt stop above pullback high, 1.7 R:R). Filled on the 3rd signal bar (13/14/16) when price was already ~25pt below the EMA — mildly extended entries in a channel bounce back to the stop more easily. Not an error; just note that later pullback-attempt fills in a channel are lower-quality than the first.

After a strong 4-bar gap-up spike, the 'channel' stalled into a tight two-sided range instead of trending. Entering the channel leg (bar6) got stopped. When the post-spike leg fails to make progress and bars start overlapping, the channel may really be an early trading range — expect chop.

Breakout long above a tight ~9pt two-sided range (bars 4-11) on a gap-up AIL day failed at the range top. Even with three rising trend-bar closes as follow-through, range-top breakouts fail often — prefer buying the low of the range / a 2nd-entry pullback, or demand a stronger, larger breakout bar.

Bought a valid H1/H2 pullback in an AIL bull channel, but entry (5794.5) was right at the session high of a channel whose spike was already 4+ bars in the past and EMA was flattening. Price gave only ~+4pts (to 5798.75) then reversed to the stop. For similar setups: a legal channel-pullback long late in an aging/grinding AIL near the session high has thin remaining reward — the target rarely gets hit. Take it if rules allow, but expect low follow-through.

Bear trend day, three consecutive bear trend bars (bar11 oversized) to a new session low; shorted the breakout bar at the low and got trapped for -1R. Remember: don't sell the 3rd trend bar into the session-low magnet right after an oversized/climactic bar — wait for a pullback toward the EMA to re-enter with-trend.

With-trend short in a stair-step bear that had already fallen ~34pts from the high, entered essentially at the fresh session low. Reversed hard on a 51-pt bull spike. Rule-abiding but poorly located — a bear channel that has run a long way into a new low is prone to a strong reversal spike; prefer entries with more room above the prior swing extreme.

Gap-up that stayed two-sided/overlapping early (eff 0.16) then formed a shallow bull channel; H2 pullback long near session highs filled and immediately reversed to stop. When the 'channel' sits on a choppy overlapping base, the pullback-long edge is weak — nothing wrong with the entry, but expect these to fail more often near range tops.

setup: trading-range-fade (bear-trend lower-high pullback short to EMA)
note: After a bear leg stalls at a fresh LL and rallies back toward the EMA making a lower high (bars 13-17 correction), fading that LH short with the session low as first target worked. Confirm it's a 2nd-entry / completed LH and that risk stays in-band; the prior session low is the natural target, not a magnet blocking the trade.

On a strong AIL trend day, sitting out the initial spike (no first-entry chasing) and waiting for the first shallow H1/H2 pullback to the rising EMA gave a with-trend entry that reached target. Reinforce: in confirmed spike-to-channel bull days, default to the 2nd-entry pullback rather than the spike.

Bear channel pullback short taken correctly WITH always-in, but the leg was already mature and price ~12pts below EMA; it stopped on the reversal. Good process; in a mature/extended channel, expect a lower hit-rate on the last pullback and don't read the loss as a rule error.

Shorting a two-legged bull pullback to the EMA in the lower third of a two-sided range (target = session-low magnet) reversed and stopped out. In a range that has gone two-sided, be skeptical of a fresh AIS short aiming at the range low — that's selling near support; prefer fading the extremes, not the middle-to-low.

Strong 5-bar bull open, bought the channel breakout near the top of the spike (~0.25pt under session high). Market stalled into overlapping/doji bars and became a two-sided triple-top range; stopped for -1.1R. Next time on a spike that starts overlapping right at its own high, treat the spike high as an overhead magnet and prefer a 2nd-entry pullback over buying the breakout into it.

setup: opening-range breakout long (first breakout after 11-bar two-sided range)
note: Bull spike (bar12) broke the morning range high; bot went long on the breakout and got stopped as price reverted into the range. First breakouts out of a long choppy two-sided range often fail — favor a 2nd-entry pullback over the initial breakout stop when efficiency has been low all morning.

AIL trend day: after an open spike faded into a two-sided range, the bot waited and took only the with-trend pullback into the rising 20-EMA once a fresh bull leg (bars12-14) reasserted always-in-long. Patience through the midday churn plus a target set at the prior session high paid off. Keep sitting out two-sided middle and re-engage on the with-trend 2nd-entry pullback when the trend leg resumes.

In a strong AIS bear channel, a with-trend L2 short after a failed 2-bar bull pullback is the right call, but a tight ~4.5pt stop just above the pullback high gets tagged on the next push up before the trend resumes — expect chop around the entry; the loss is noise, keep taking these.
